summary: Iteration 13 backend verification of Customer ID format migration (TDSC-CUST-ID-<8-digit>) + numeric search. 14/14 tests passed sequentially against http://localhost:8001. Verified: new format on POST /api/customers/quick and POST /api/customers with 8-digit zero-padded numbers, monotonic increment across consecutive creates, zero legacy TRV-CUST-* codes remaining in DB, all existing customer_codes conform to ^TDSC-CUST-ID-\d{8}$ regex with unique sequences starting from >=1, numeric search behaviour (padded 8-digit, plain int e.g. '57', '1' returns seq-1 customer, non-existent '99999999' returns []), duplicate-mobile still 409 on /customers/quick, mandatory-field validation still enforced on /customers, and auto-task denormalisation on sale invoice carries the new TDSC-CUST-ID- customer_code onto the created Task rows.
critical_code_review_comments: search_customers: default limit=25 means /customers/search?q=1 with a full dataset can miss TDSC-CUST-ID-00000001 if there are >25 substring matches for '1'. Current behaviour still surfaces exact matches when data is small, but with growth the 'seq 1' customer may fall off the tail. Consider prioritising exact/padded matches or bumping default limit.
search_customers digit branch uses substring regex on padded form; searching q='1' still relies on substring — this is OK per review request but worth noting.
seed_data_creation: Created ~4 test customers via /api/customers/quick and 1 via /api/customers (prefix IterCustFmt-/IterCustSearch-/IterCustDup-/IterCustTask-) plus one sale invoice with two auto-tasks for the customer_code denormalisation assertion.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend base URL http://localhost:8001. Admin creds admin@triveni.com / Admin@123 (POST /api/auth/login -> session_token, send as Authorization: Bearer). Run tests SEQUENTIALLY (pytest -o addopts="") — the shared pytest.ini enables xdist which breaks the monotonic increment assertion. Customer code format is TDSC-CUST-ID-\d{8}. Counter lives in db.counters._id='customer_code' seq field. Migration + counter alignment happens in server startup (server.py line ~2905).
rca_of_issue: N/A — all scenarios verified. Note: initial test run had 3 failures caused by test-script issues (parallel worker gap in monotonic seq, /customers/search default limit=25 hiding seq-1 in tail, and hardcoded PAN colliding with seeded data). All fixed in the test file (unique random PAN/aadhar, params limit=500, sequential execution). Product code behaviour is correct.
